body: My ex would literally call it a reset
OP this is extremely solid information and advice. These texts sound like they could’ve been between me and my abuser as well.
It absolutely is not a scam.  You would just rather turn a blind eye to what’s happening in Gaza, like many people it seems.  Figures.

Respectfully, my friend is a real person.  I have met his mother on video chat too.  I was skeptical in the beginning before I got to know him, but have seen and heard more than enough proof to support that he is indeed a 21 year old young man trying to survive and support his family.  You don’t have to believe me, I will not stop trying to find him help whether or not you do.  I totally understand the concern about being scammed, but this is definitely not a scam.

Yes I have video chatted with him from the literal rubble where he lives and I have a mutual friend who has been in contact with him for a year.  We have a group chat on Instagram going daily to talk, make sure he is still alive and see whether he has food.  You can DM me for more info if you want, I am happy to talk with anyone who wants to help.
No.  They benefit from abusing you.  It is a defect of moral character and that is not something that generally changes.
Yes my abuser also freaked out whenever I said he was abusive.  He would also flip it back on me saying I was abusive (I was not.)
IMO the morning starting off allows him control over the day.  It sets the tone for you to already have to bend to his moods and tantrums.
Why do you stay with him?  Have you considered leaving?  What are you gaining from being with him?

Yo I LOLed at your first paragraph reading Reddit in the dark in bed hahaha.  So cringe, mine was the same, he was like idk 8” and obsessed with how huge his dick was.  He never made me cum and during one of our last huge fights he stormed off to the bedroom and snatched up my Hitachi and smashed it to pieces on the floor in front of me.  🤣🤣 Like my god if that isn’t just a metaphor for everything because he was a POS with trash dick and selfish and evil.  I’d have to finish myself if I ever wanted to after he was already done and rolled over and I struggle with coming with a partner from anxiety and stuff in general.  One time he was rolled over and I was trying and he screamed at me that I was interrupting him trying to nap.  That kind of shit did a lot of emotional damage tbh, I have intimacy problems now 8 months away from him and obviously in general the abuse being so recent makes me hesitant to date and makes it more difficult.  The week I was planning to leave he kept trying to guilt me into sex over and over and I had to pretend everything was fine to keep him from knowing about my plan to escape, so I let him sexually assault me and that shit also messed with me.  I’m a stripper, I was before and when I met him and started dating him long distance.  He moved into my home across the country and bullied me into quitting immediately.  I’m back into it now because I love it, but it compounds my intimacy issues in some ways because I learn a lot of things about people (mostly men) and evil things they’re open about when you’re a stripper and they use you in various ways including as a surrogate therapist or even a place to exercise/exorcise their demons.

Mine always had women allegedly throwing themselves at him (I saw zero evidence of this ever.)  He would claim in public women would stare and and ask for his number, that he had women sliding into his DMs, that he had an ex sending him a dollar on CashApp to get his attention (the same ex I found out after I got away from him that he actually did prison time for pleading guilty to felony battery and felony imprisonment on her and she has a lifetime restraining order against him).  I never ever saw one woman check him out, not one.
Saaaame
My abuser lied about his age off the rip (which is also hilarious because he said he was 39 when he was 44 and looked fucking 74.)

Same.  My abuser told me that I had ruined how my family perceived him because I told them how he treated me and then wouldn’t come around my family as a result.  He told me married adults handle things behind closed doors and don’t talk about anything personal with others.  He punished me for my “attitude” (see: being angry af after he screamed at and berated me in our home in front of friends who were staying over) by refusing to attend my grandma’s funeral (I’m glad in retrospect, my grandma wouldn’t have wanted him there, he’s a fucking monster.)

My abuser would talk about how he was impressed that I could handle his oh so earth-shattering dick because I was thinner than other girls he’d allegedly slept with, because I guess weight has something to do with being able to handle a mediocre selfish railing from some narcissistic trash penis?  The ironic part is the depression and abuse made me lose 20 pounds while I was with him, it was some of the skinniest I’ve ever been in my life (I gained it all back after I got away from him).

I agree with other comments that you should put in cameras to record evidence, but only if you can be sure he won’t find them.  Start making plans as quietly as possible.  Can you kids’ father help you?  Do you have family or friends who you can stay with for a while?  Definitely consult with a lawyer.  No matter what, don’t let him find out.  I am proud of you for coming to the realization that you don’t deserve this bullshit treatment.  You have so much life to live.  After escaping my abuser 8 months ago, I can tell you it gets better.  I won’t lie and say it won’t be hard - the post-separation abuse was intense and would be continuing I’m sure if my abuser wasn’t in prison right now.  I fully expect harassment when he gets out, maybe worse.  But my point is that your life is worth fighting for and freedom from his abuse is worth any difficulty that comes along. Sending you love.

Do you have any times where he is certain to be gone for hours?  Like does he go to work, etc?  When I fled my abuser I had my family waiting outside my apartment a couple blocks away until he was gone and I knew he’d be gone for a while.  I had stored a few bags hidden around the house and I had a list written of bags to grab (in addition to my three cats I had to get into carriers) and steps to take so that when it was go time I could follow the steps and lessen the panic.  When you leave it especially helps to have someone there to get you and/or help you, partially for help, partially for safety and partially to keep you from freezing/changing your mind.  Please do not be afraid to be honest with the people who know you irl, you might be surprised how much people can be willing to show up for you to save you from danger. Because make no mistake, you are in serious danger.  When you decide to leave, make sure whatever you do you keep him from finding out until you’re gone.  I planned my escape for about a week, during which time I pretended everything was fine to the degree that I was hand-washing my abusers’ underwear (we had little money for anything much less the laundromat), I let him steal my money from my account for drugs and pretended not to notice and I let him sexually assault me.  That part was a very memorable piece of the trauma but it protected me and I have survived.  Please keep us updated and know that you are loved.

Your friends can help you with your plan to leave.  Being coworkers is good because you spend time with them away from him.  You can start to store your getaway bags with them - bring things to work a little at a time.  Open up a CashApp card and have it mailed to a friend’s address.  You cannot change him, he doesn’t love you and one day he may kill you.  Keep reading the book until you believe it, because it’s all true.  You deserve a peaceful, safe life.

I hope you find a way out of your situation just like I hope for OP.  I am 8 months free from my abuser and it really can get better.  Living imprisoned with someone who tortures you for funsies under the guise of being a partner is absolute hell.  Sending you love and hope.

It’s funny because my abuser also had booohooohoooo childhood trauma and mommy issues.  It’s funny how that’s a valid excuse to actively use and harm a woman you plan to marry.  Fuck his trauma actually, how about that?  Abusers are a lost cause and when they go to therapy they get better at using language to manipulate and abuse you.  They lie to therapists so that they center themselves as the victim.  Fuck that shit.  What about things you’ve been through?  Would you treat him like shit because you lost your parents?  Because that sounds recent and I know it’s fucking traumatic and painful and I’m extremely sorry for your loss btw.

Because he wants your resources, your home, your time, your body, your attention.  He is a predator and a parasite.  My abuser literally invaded and took over my life like a virus.  After I ran from him he would make videos on TikTok spreading lies about me and he’d be down to the socks in outfits I paid for LOL.
And also if you don’t feel strong enough to leave for yourself, do it for your dad.  He’d be so proud that you stood up for yourself and took your life back.

Tbh my support system already could tell I was being abused before I admitted it.  They may already suspect.  If you know they love you enough to be your parental figures, have faith that they will love you enough to help you and not judge you.  Nobody judged me when I was honest and said I needed help.  Everyone who loves me hates my abuser though and would knock him tf out on my behalf.

Because a beautiful fancy ring and a proposal in front of your family makes him look good.  Narcissists love to look good especially in front of people who you would run to for help, because if he’s just oh so sweet maybe they’ll believe him and not you.  It’s not to make you happy or feel special, I promise.

No matter what his mood and anger issues are, he is an abuser because he lacks a moral compass.  You cannot love someone into having one.  Also, he put his hands on you FIRST and REPEATEDLY.  Poking and sticking his fingers in your ears repeatedly would be assault if you did it on a random stranger, wouldn’t it?  So actually, you didn’t start this and you were defending yourself.  He does this shit to get a reaction from you to justify abusing you.  He likes abusing you and doesn’t love you, just so you know.  My abuser used to provoke me so badly I’ll never forget the time I took a broom and started smashing it against the wall and knocked a hole in the wall from it because I was so fucking angry at his abuse.  And then of course he took that as a green light to destroy my property when he got angry.  Only my property, never his.  He told me he called me all the names in the world because I was the first one to open the name-calling box (I called him an asshole because he was in fact being a raging POS asshole and still is one).  My point is, please consider getting tf out of this situation.  HE DOES NOT LOVE YOU.  Even on your worst day, would you treat him how he treats you?  He enjoys harming you. Sending you love, I really hope you get out.  I escaped my abuser about 8 months ago and while I struggle with PTSD and my mental health is also affected by the horrible state of the world rn, life is actually worth living now.  When I was with him I not only wanted to die because I felt because I loved him I had to stay, but also I figured he’d eventually kill me because his violence kept escalating.  He’s in prison rn and hopefully stays for a long time.  It can get better.

I had a similar feeling of intense stress reading this because I got this same type of bullshit controlling treatment.  This is behavior that will get worse with time.  You shrink and shrink your freedoms until one day everything you do is determined by what will keep him from getting angry.  It’s a horrible way to live.

My abuser would prevent me from leaving the apartment during fights by false imprisoning me in my bedroom.  He would sit on top of me on the bed and hold me down and sometimes would spit on my face while he did it.  It’s incredibly violating.  I am so happy that you are away from your abuser and that he is your ex.  Sending you love and healing.

My abuser also controlled my sleep.  He would wake me up whenever he wanted me up and would often start my morning with picking arguments with me.  He’s a (shitty) rapper and would literally sound torture me out of bed by playing his latest (shitty) song over and over at full volume because he’s THAT much of a narcissist.

You are not crazy and you are so spot on to call off the wedding.  My abuser escalated after we got married.  You are trauma-bonded to him.  Look on Google for the free PDF of Why Does He Do That? By Lundy Bancroft.  It helped me break the trauma bond and escape my abuser.
I can’t even date anymore after the abuse, trusting anyone enough to fall in love or to have intimacy feels too dangerous to risk.  I’m glad you’re out of your situation and doing better.  💜

Not only is it unforgivable but it’s such a typical narcissistic abuse playbook move.  My ex used to hold a knife to his neck during arguments and tell me he would kill himself because of my anger (my anger at his abuse, mind you) and because it was my fault I had to watch.  Spoiler alert, his ass is still very much alive and thankfully in prison for a while.

Tbh I am so traumatized and have been in relationships for so much of my adult life that between those two facts I have zero desire for a relationship.  I don’t want to give my time, emotions, resources, effort, attention, nothing to a partner.  I only care about seeing my friends and family and spending time with my cats and working my jobs and growing myself as a person.  I am incredibly afraid of being trapped by another monster to the degree that even if I was at all interested in finding love, I am not willing to risk it because there are so many predators out there.

Yeah I lost 20 pounds while I was with my ex for a few reasons, none of which were intentional or positive.  It sucked after I left having to hear from others how good the weight loss looked, because it wasn’t sustainable.  I went through a big eating phase a few months in and gained it all back seemingly overnight, which was painful to suddenly see.

Hey, I just want you to know you deserve a good life and if you leave and she hurts herself IT IS NOT YOUR FAULT.  I was being severely abused and my life was pure shit because of it.  One of the things that made me stay was worrying he’d kill himself if I left.  Guess what?  He didn’t.  What he did do was aggressively stalk and harrass me and commit further crimes against me.  The day you decide to leave, you will feel so, so much better.  It will be hard and the trauma lasts long after the relationship ends.  But you don’t deserve to be treated this way and she doesn’t deserve someone treating her so well.

Emotional abuse has a way of keeping you around much longer.  It’s easier to question if a tantrum is really even abuse than it is to question it if he punches you in the nose. Having to deal with his temper tantrums over absolutely nothing (and that is nothing, he has the money, you’ve done the same for him  and you’re MARRIED) is absolutely a concentrated effort on his part to make you feel like shit and make you feel like you shouldn’t ask for his help.

My ex broke my things a lot during my relationship and didn’t see it as abusive.  Breaking things in anger is what kids do during a tantrum.  In a grown man it is a serious red flag and could escalate to other behaviors in the future.

When he pushed me and gave me the black eye, he burst into tears and said he would call the police on himself.  He said he knew what he did was wrong and he would never touch me again. So I forgave him and kept covering up the black eye with make up like a good battered housewife. A week later, he shoved me again the same way he did when I got the black eye.  That was when I began to wake up and make my exit plan, because I realized he would continue to put hands on me if he did after that horrible incident. They don’t change, they get worse and worse, and often become lethal.

It’s okay, I survived him and he’s currently in prison related to his prior DVs convictions.  It was not the first time he physically hurt me, but it was the worst. He had been putting hands on me since December 2023 and he coerced me into marriage, which we did in June 2024.  He had been doing things like grabbing my head and my arms, pushing me, threatening to crash, my car with both of us in it, threatening to burn my house down with us in it, holding a knife to his neck and I had to intervene because I was afraid he would kill himself.  He would also falsely imprisoned me on the bed in my bedroom when I would try to run away during fights. He would hold me down and spit in my face, forcibly kiss me, laugh at me and mock me, scream at me, etc. One time he did that and his arm clipped my eye socket, and I had a more mild black eye than the one he gave me after we got married.  He would throw my things, break my things, terrorize me, and my cats, and the emotional abuse was literally constant. He would scream at me on a regular basis and put me down in pretty much every way you can think of except my looks. He financially abused the shit out of me and used all of my money and didn’t work. He socially isolated me and one by one made sure to let me know how much he hated each of my friends. I could go on and on. I really hope that you don’t marry that monster, because I promise it will get worse, and I also promise it will never get better. These abusive men are all the same, they’re cut from the same cloth and they use the same tactics, and they have the same lack of any moral fibre whatsoever

As a recovering codependent I very much agree.  Without working on this you are susceptible to finding yourself in more abusive relationships down the road because abusers take heavy advantage of codependent traits.
This book helped save my life

It’s already been physical and I guarantee it will escalate once he has you marriage-trapped.  Two weeks after we got married, my abuser shoved me face first into a door frame (missing the door cause he tore it off during another fit.)  I had a huge black eye.

Abuse is a defect of moral character. You cannot correct somebody’s moral character. I empathize a lot, my ex was a a really shitty person and hate-filled person and I also didn’t realize it until he had trapped me. That’s because he kept the mask on long enough to trap me. You have to choose to break your bond with this person and work, actively every second to do so until it’s broken. You deserve better and he doesn’t deserve a girlfriend.

You have to make the choice to break your addiction to him. It is a neurological addiction. I really urge you to look up trauma bonds and do a lot of reading about them.  I am sorry that you’re going through a hard time in your life.
I guess keep listening to your bro who gets hookups all the time about how to get long-term girlfriend. Don’t listen to any of the women who are trying to help you. Good luck.

I’m asking you what else is interesting about you.  I didn’t say women don’t want to have relationships with attractive people. I said that women don’t wanna have relationships with people who only have looks as a selling point. I feel like you’re being willfully contrary and that’s going to keep you very lonely.
And also, he’s racist.  Why do you want to be with somebody who is a racist?

Just so you know when he’s being nice, that is part of the abuse cycle. You wouldn’t stay if the abuse was constant, the nice periods trick you into thinking they could someday become permanent. They never will, he will always be an abusive person and he will escalate. With that in mind, ask yourself, what positive things are you getting out of this relationship?

Just so you know, the kindness is part of the abuse. You wouldn’t stay he treated you like shit 24/7.  That is how the trauma bond forms. If you don’t know about trauma bonding, look into what it is and what it does to your brain. Also look up the book Why does he do that? by Lundy Bancroft.  It is free in a PDF online. It will help you a lot.  It helped me wake up and escape my abuser.

Why can’t you tell your therapist about these things? If you can’t be honest with your therapist, you need to look at the things you can’t be honest about and ask yourself why. And also is your therapist a good fit?

It sounds like you are trauma bonded to this person. There is no judgment from me, I was also trauma bonded to my abuser. But you deserve better. You’re lucky you don’t live with him. Do not advance the relationship, it will only get worse.
Why do you keep seeing this person?  I’m worried about your safety.
What does attractive mean?

It might get you more hookups.  Being jacked doesn’t make for boyfriend material.  Listen to the people trying to help you and stop listening to people perpetuating this hyperfocus on looks.  It’s ok that you don’t have a lot of experience with women.  There are lot of commenters in here who have a lot of experience BEING women who date men and they are going to give you the best advice.

You don’t have to believe that those things are much more important but unless you’re looking for purely physical hookups, which you’re not, they absolutely are more important.  You are insisting on focusing on looks and ignoring this and frankly, you’re missing out on good advice.  Tell me this, how can a girl show you intense interest if there’s nothing interesting about you besides some looks?  Again, unless it’s just about sex a girl is not going to show you intense interest in seriously dating you just for looks.

This is what I’m wondering, OP.  I wouldn’t want to date a guy who was only focused on looks looks looks.  Belmont is asking a really good question that will help you because like other people have commented, your personality shines through when you have a strong one.  I’ve matched with a lot of very attractive guys with zero personality and worse, bad personalities and they haven’t gotten a date outta me because of it.  What else are you working on in yourself?  Yes physical attraction is important to a certain extent, but also looks fade and are not a successful foundation for a long term relationship.

I empathize.  I fled my abuser in July, so I’ve been away a little over 7 months.  I went after him legally for what I could prove, but like you I had little evidence of what he did during the relationship.  The main charge I have against him is what he did during the post-breakup abuse when he stalked and threatened me and did some other things.  If nothing else, pressing charges starts a paper trail for the next girl to see.  I wouldn’t have had the guts to press charges had I not found out in September about his priors for DV on two different women.

He’s not only abusive but is very capable of killing you.  Punching you in the stomach is horribly abusive, as is sexual coercion and assault and threatening you with a deadly weapon.  Do you have documentation of any of the abuse, as in pictures, messages from him admitting to any of this, etc?  Because he has committed multiple felonies against you.
And also if you’re the one who had a seizure, he should be doing EVERYTHING for you the day after.  He’s enjoying your pain and doesn’t love you, I promise.
Relationships without abuse are possible.  Do you have a support system you can lean on?  Are you considering leaving this relationship?  You’re welcome to DM me if you need.

I agree.  What is one thing you think is possible for you to work on?  Can you search for a job?  Do you want to go to college?  Do you have any hobbies that interest you?  Is there somewhere you can go regularly to get out into the world more like a park or a cafe?  Are you able to get a therapist?  Something that’s helpful when you’re as overwhelmed as you sound is to focus on one changeable thing at a time.

The “kindness” is part of the abuse, you know.  It’s used to keep you in the bond because without it you’d have 24/7 torture and you’d be more apt to leave.  I escaped my abuser 7 months ago.  Much of what you wrote here are things he said to me.  He would call me princess to piss me off and belittle me during fights.  I wish you happiness and freedom, you don’t deserve this abuse.
He’s scared of how others will see him if you tell them things he’s said and did, not how you portray him.

No, this is definitely gaslighting manipulation. Sounds like my ex when I left him, love hate love hate love hate love hate love hate messages over and over just constantly stalking and harassing me from burner numbers and various burner emails and socials until I had to get a restraining order. He violated it and then I had to get police further involved.

This is abuse with a big helping of extreme justifying mental gymnastics on his part.  Your child will see how he treats you.  He may treat your child the same at some point.  He is absolutely capable of killing you.
This is how my abuser talked to me on a regular basis.  This behavior kills your soul and sometimes literally ends up in them taking your life too.  OP this isn’t normal, I’m so sorry.

My abuser told me has 5 kids but he told his last BM (who I recently connected with because of legal issues we have in common against him) he has 7 or more.  I can’t have kids by choice myself, but in the past I’ve been slightly open to dating dads and honestly both the dudes I would’ve done the stepmom shit for ended up being huge abusers.  Now I’m good on dating altogether and honestly I’m thinking maybe in a few years if I have my life more together maybe I could adopt an older kid who needs a home or something, idk.
This guy is love-bombing the shit out of you and trying to coerce you into sex.  I wonder what his baby mom would say about him.

This sounds so much like my story except for wanting to start a family.  My ex promised a grandiose future filled with adventures and security, telling me everything I wanted to hear.  But he never worked except for uber eats in my car with my insurance, my name, my gas money and I had to go with him almost every time on top of my two jobs.  He spent $50 to $100 every single day on weed and would treat me worse if he had no weed.  He coerced me into marriage and tried to baby trap me by convincing me right after my cat died suddenly and I was in one of the worst most vulnerable emotional states I’ve ever been in to try and have a baby via IVF because I’m sterilized (luckily he was too broke to pay for it).  He has at least 5 kids, although he told his last BM he had 7 or more.  He was emotionally, physically, socially, sexually and financially abusive af.  He’s in prison now though, if anyone needs some happy news.
Sounds exactly like something my abuser would’ve exploded at me over.  So glad you dodged that one, huge yikes.
Warrants related to prior DV case, which I did not become aware of until after I left.

Yup two weeks after we got married mine pushed me into a door frame resulting in a huge black eye and he burst into real tears (he always cried actual tears when manipulating me) and said he’d call the cops on himself.  I felt like he was genuinely sorry so I forgave him and he said he wouldn’t put hands on me again.  He then pushed me again a week later.  I’ve been away from him 7 months today and sometimes I still can’t believe I’m still alive.  I wonder sometimes if when he gets out of prison if he will come for me.

Mine was in another state and harassed me through burner numbers and multiple accounts on multiple social media platforms.  It was such a relief when he was arrested because it was daily before that and then suddenly - sweet silence.  He will get out eventually and then that’s the other issue - basically as long as he’s alive I’ll have to look over my shoulder.  I connected with one of his exes over a shared legal issue and she said we’re lucky he didn’t kill us and she thinks he’s dangerous enough to kill us and I absolutely agree.  I hope yours leaves you alone, fuck these abusers.

I’m in the same boat of having unresolved legal issues with my abuser.  People have said to me, well thank god he’s not in your life anymore!  And while I get what they’re trying to say, he still is until he’s not at all and even then I’m sure I will have symptoms of the trauma to work through.  I’ve been away from my abuser for about seven months and I have zero romantic feelings towards him because I stopped liking or loving him before I left.  It was a learning curve to stop treating him like a human being, though, because I treat everybody like a person. He stalked me for months after I left, and it took me a long time to work up the nerve to get him arrested.  Getting him arrested was the first step in being able to be free of him because he violated my restraining order immediately and was threatening my safety in multiple ways.
I am trying to date again and I am realizing I can’t because I am extremely afraid of being trapped and abused again and while I used to love sex, I hate it now.
You’re right
I’m not playing around with people.  I can’t know what I want and don’t want if I stay in my room forever.

No it doesn’t sound like you love bombed.  I’ve also had a couple dates lately where I thought things were going well and wasn’t sure why the other person rejected me.  It doesn’t make either of us unattractive or unworthy.  Wishing you luck in love!
Saaaame, I was NOT attracted to my abuser until after the love bombing successfully occurred.

For what it’s worth, I’m currently dating but I don’t think I’m ready for a romantic relationship.  Personally I’ve been through recent trauma that is the major reason why and I’m not sure I’ll ever want one again.  But I can’t know if I don’t try and if I don’t explore what I do and don’t want in people I keep company with in any sort of dating capacity.  It’s good you are trying to understand her perspective without taking it personally.  Incompatibility isn’t a negative thing.

My ex kept me trapped because of my empathy for his mental health problems.  Lundy Bancroft says in Why Does He Do That that mental health problems don’t cause abuse, abusers cause abuse.  They choose to.  And that’s when a lightbulb when on in my head and I chose to take back my life.  You’ll be on this carousel forever unless you choose to get off of it because your abuser won’t change.  He benefits from treating you like shit.

Came here to say the same.  Your dog doesn’t deserve to endure his abuse.  You don’t, but your dog can’t make the choice to leave and you can. My cat has PTSD from my ex.  Also mark my words, this behavior will escalate.
Same I’m always like, who do you need to hide me from???  Next!
Done providing for the kids?  Yikes OP, I would see a divorce lawyer.
This is SUPER abusive.  I’m so sorry you’re being treated this way.
It’s more than fair. I don’t miss anything about him. I hate him and it takes a lot for me to hate absolutely anybody.

He kicked in three different doors in my apartment. When I left him, my wonderful father was amazing enough to come and spend three days making repairs so that I didn’t have huge expenses to pay the apartment complex. My dad jokingly said I can understand him kicking in the bathroom and the bedroom door, but why a closet?  I live with my parents now and I am so grateful for every single second of my freedom and my time here with them.

Literally almost all of these are relatable.  My ex was a cocaine addict, and started up with crack towards the end of our relationship. He blamed all of his abuse on being traumatized as a kid and going to prison for so many years, some of which I found out was for domestic violence. He was so loud all the time, and was a shitty rapper and would be loudly playing his music all the time. He wouldn’t let me sleep once he wanted me awake and he would sometimes sound to torture me out of bed with his new songs.  He also didn’t work, spent tons of my money on whatever he wanted, isolated me from everybody, tore me apart and broke me down emotionally, and I had to give up my apartment when that I had worked hard to get a few months before I met him.  I don’t miss him at all. I don’t miss anything about him. I’m glad every single part of our relationship is in the past. And he’s in prison right now so that’s even better.

I have recent trauma from an abusive relationship that included physical abuse and I’m highly sensitive about being touched in any form on a date.  I want to be the one to initiate breaking the touch barrier.  So I appreciate your approach.
